```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gtsummary)
library(here)
library(gt)

adsl <- read_csv(
    here("data", "processed", "adsl_clean.csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
)
trt <- intersect(c("trt01p", "trt01a"), names(adsl))[1]
required <- c("usubjid", "age", "sex", trt)
if (any(is.na(trt)) || !all(required %in% names(adsl))) stop("Confirm ADSL mappings in docs/data_dictionary.md")
```

# Summary and Conclusions

## Introduction

This notebook describes the baseline characteristics of participants enrolled in the clinical trial using the processed ADSL dataset created in Notebook 1.

The objective was to assess whether the treatment groups were comparable before treatment was administered. Establishing baseline comparability is important because it helps ensure that any differences observed during the study are more likely to be associated with the treatment rather than pre-existing differences between groups.

---

## Analyses Performed

The following baseline characteristics were summarised:

- Number of participants per treatment group
- Age
- Sex
- Race
- Body Mass Index (BMI)
- Education level

A publication-style baseline characteristics table (Table 1) was produced using the `gtsummary` package. Participant counts were also visualised using a bar chart.

---

## Results

The three treatment groups contained similar numbers of participants:

- Placebo: 86 participants
- Xanomeline High Dose: 84 participants
- Xanomeline Low Dose: 84 participants

Median age was similar across all treatment groups, indicating comparable age distributions.

The proportions of male and female participants were also broadly comparable, with only minor variation between groups.

Most participants were White, with smaller numbers of Black or African American participants and one American Indian or Alaska Native participant.

Overall, no substantial demographic imbalances were observed between treatment groups.

---

## Outputs Produced

This notebook generated:

- Baseline characteristics table (Table 1)
- Participant distribution bar chart
- HTML version of Table 1

These outputs provide the demographic foundation for the efficacy and safety analyses performed in later notebooks.

---

## Conclusion

The baseline analysis indicates that the randomisation process produced treatment groups with similar demographic characteristics. The groups appear sufficiently comparable to support subsequent efficacy and safety analyses.

The next stage of the project focuses on evaluating treatment effectiveness using longitudinal ADAS-Cog measurements collected throughout the clinical trial.
